prompts.access.simplify.short: Simplify this text while keeping its meaning: [text]
prompts.access.simplify.detailed: Rewrite the text in plain language for [audience]. Rules: short sentences, one idea per sentence, everyday words, terms explained in brackets, actions as a list. Keep all facts, numbers, deadlines and conditions. At the end, list what you cut from the original. Text: [text]
prompts.access.simplify.refine: Are there words in my text that are still hard? Suggest replacements.
prompts.access.simplify.check: Ask 3 questions about the simplified text to check it's understandable.
prompts.access.short.short: Make a short version of the text in 3–5 points: [text]
prompts.access.short.detailed: Make a short version for people who find long texts hard. At the top, the main point in one sentence. Then 3–5 points: what's important to know, what to do and by when. A “more details” pointer to the full text. Add nothing that's not in the original. Text: [text]
prompts.access.short.refine: Make an even shorter version for an SMS or notification.
prompts.access.short.check: Is there a condition in the full text without which the short version could mislead?
prompts.access.steps.detailed: Rewrite as instructions for [audience]. Rules: numbered steps, one action per step, start with a verb, say what the person will see after each step, don't rely only on “left”, “right” or “the red button” (may not work for blind or colour-blind users) — include the button's name. Text: [text]
prompts.access.steps.refine: Add what to do if something goes wrong at step [number].
prompts.access.steps.check: Here's how I understood the instructions: [summary]. Where could a reader go wrong?
prompts.access.glossary.short: Explain the terms in this text in plain words: [text]
prompts.access.glossary.detailed: Find every word in the text that might be unclear to [audience]: jargon, abbreviations, officialese, foreign words. Table: word, plain explanation (up to 15 words), example. Spell out abbreviations. Text: [text]
prompts.access.glossary.refine: Which of these words could simply be replaced in the text with plainer ones?
prompts.access.glossary.check: I'll explain [term] in my own words: [explanation]. Is it accurate?
prompts.access.image.short: Help me describe an image for blind readers: [what's in the image]
prompts.access.image.detailed: Help me describe an image. What's in it: [what's in the image]. Where it's used and why: [context]. Make 2 versions: short (up to 125 characters, for alt) and detailed (3–5 sentences: from general to detail, any important text in the image word for word, colours only if they matter).
prompts.access.image.refine: It's a diagram or chart. How can I convey the data as text or a table?
prompts.access.image.check: Would someone who can't see the image understand why it's there from my description: [description]?
prompts.access.structure.short: Suggest a clear structure for this document: [text]
prompts.access.structure.detailed: Suggest a document structure that works for everyone, including screen-reader users. Heading levels in order (no skipped levels), short sections, lists instead of long inline enumerations, tables only for tabular data, descriptive link text instead of “click here”. Text: [text]
prompts.access.structure.refine: Rewrite the link texts so it's clear where they go: [links]
prompts.access.structure.check: Here are my headings: [headings]. Can you understand the document from them alone?
prompts.access.subtitles.detailed: Format subtitles for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers from the transcript: no more than 2 lines, break by meaning, the speaker's name when it changes (if it's not visible who's talking), and meaningful sounds in round brackets, e.g. (laughter), (music fades). Text: [text]
prompts.access.subtitles.refine: Make a simplified subtitle version for people who read slowly.
prompts.access.subtitles.check: Which sounds that matter for understanding are missing from my subtitles? [subtitles and video description]
prompts.access.screenreader.short: What in this text is awkward for a screen reader? [text]
prompts.access.screenreader.detailed: Check the text for screen-reader friendliness: emoji and symbols used instead of words, tables used for layout, abbreviations a reader will mispronounce, links without descriptions, information conveyed only by colour or position. For each problem, a fixed version. Text: [text]
prompts.access.screenreader.refine: How should I format a social post with hashtags so a screen reader reads it properly?
prompts.access.screenreader.check: I've fixed the text: [text]. Are there any problems left?
prompts.access.reading.short: Rewrite the text for a [age or level] reader: [text]
prompts.access.reading.detailed: Assess how hard the text is for [audience], then rewrite it for that level. First: sentence length, share of difficult words, abstract ideas without examples. Then a new version: average sentence length under 12 words, concrete examples, all facts kept. Text: [text]
prompts.access.reading.refine: Make 2 versions: for a beginner reader and for an adult learning the language.
prompts.access.reading.check: Which parts of the new version became inaccurate through simplification?
prompts.access.feedback.short: What should I ask users to check the accessibility of [material]?
prompts.access.feedback.detailed: I've made [material] for [audience]. Help me plan a test with 2–3 people from that audience: tasks for them to do, 8 follow-up questions (what was hard, where they got confused, what they'd change), how to record observations without personal data, how to invite and thank them politely.
prompts.access.feedback.refine: How can I run this test if participants can't come in person?
prompts.access.feedback.check: Here's what participants said: [observations]. What should I fix first?

verify.access.simplify: Compare the simplified text with the original fact by fact. In official documents, keep key wording verbatim.
verify.access.short: It's easy to lose a condition or exception in a short version. Check those separately.
verify.access.steps: Follow the instructions yourself or ask someone from the audience to: that reveals missing steps.
verify.access.glossary: Explanations must be accurate, not just simple. Check them against a reliable source.
verify.access.image: The AI can't see the image if you only described it. Check the description matches the picture.
verify.access.structure: Check the structure with a screen reader or the heading navigation in your editor.
verify.access.subtitles: Check the subtitles against the video: names, terms and numbers are often misrecognised.
verify.access.screenreader: The best check is listening to the text with your phone's or computer's built-in screen reader.
verify.access.reading: Reading level is only a guide. Testing on someone from the target audience works best.
verify.access.feedback: No checklist replaces the views of the people you're making it for. Ask them.
